question.leadin: This 18th century ruler issued a decree that created the Smolny [SMOHL-nee] Institute of Noble Maidens, the first public European learning institution for girls.
question.text: Name this Russian empress, whose collaboration with many Enlightenment thinkers earned her the nickname "Enlightened Despot."
question.clue: Odessa was established during the reign of this ruler, who conquered Crimea during a war with the Ottomans.

swap.text: This city that sits on both sides of the Dnieper ("duh-NEE-per") River is home to the St. Sophia Cathedral and the historic Golden Gate. It is the capital of the Ukraine.
swap.clue: It's not Novgorod, but a grand prince of this city was named Yaroslav the Wise.

question.text: Josef Stalin renamed Petrograd after this communist, his predecessor as leader of the Soviets. He led the October Revolution with Leon Trotsky to depose the Romanov dynasty from power.
question.clue: An online poll is asking civilians to vote whether or not to bury his body, which is presently displayed in Red Square.

swap.text: The House of Romanov came to an end with the Revolution of 1917, when this last Russian czar abdicated. The Bolsheviks killed still him and his family at the Ipatiev House.
swap.clue: This man's finance minister negotiated the end to a war with Japan in the Treaty of Portsmuth, and was named Sergei Witte.

question.text: The port of Sevastopol was later besieged in this 1850s war, which was fought over a peninsula on the Black Sea.
question.clue: During this war the French victory at the Battle of Malakoff ended the Siege of Sevastopol, and miscommunication between Lord Raglan and Lord Cardigan caused the Charge of the Light Brigade at the Battle of Balaclava.

swap.leadin: Name these other people who survived assassination attempts.
swap.text: This General Secretary of the Communist Party in the Soviet Union was almost killed by Soviet Army deserter Vikoty Ilyin. He was succeeded in his post by Yuri Andropov.
swap.clue: His economic policies have been described as "the lowest stage of socialism," and this man is remembered for recognizing postwar European boundaries with the Helsinki Accords.

question.leadin: This state was founded by Oleg of Novgorod and christianized by Vladimir the Great.
question.text: Name this confederation ruled by the Rurik dynasty in modern-day Ukraine, often considered a predecessor to the Russian empire.
question.clue: Its leaders used a system of succession in which the throne would pass to the eldest brother of the deceased, called the rota or "ladder" system.

swap.leadin: During this conflict, the Green armies were formed by peasants to prevent other belligerents from requisitioning supplies from their villages.
swap.text: Name this conflict in which one side utilized "war communism" to defeat the White Army. That victorious side also briefly allied with and later attacked the Black Army of anarchist Nestor Makhno during this conflict.
swap.clue: "War communism" was implemented by the winners of this conflict to ensure supplies for its army.

question.leadin: Conspiracy theories held that this ruler became a hermit named Feodor Kuzmich after his mysterious death from typhus in Taganrog.
question.text: Name this tsar, the first one advised by liberal statesman Mikhail Speransky. This tsar conquered Finland and granted a constitution to Poland.
question.clue: After his nation lost the Battle of Friedland, he met with Napoleon on a raft in the Niemen River to sign the Treaty of Tilsit.

swap.text: He summoned the first zemski sobor, an assembly of clergy, gentry, and boyars, and he also established a secret police called the oprichniki. For 15 points, name this Rurikid dynasty monarch.
swap.answerHtml: Ivan the Terrible [or Ivan IV; or Ivan Grozny; prompt on Ivan]
swap.clue: This ruler created his nation's first standing army, the Streltsy, as well as a secret police force called the Oprichnina.

question.text: Along with Kamenev, this politician was executed after the Trial of the Sixteen. A letter purportedly sent by this man to the British Communist party may have cost Ramsay Macdonald's Labour party the 1924 election.
question.clue: As Prosecutor General, Vyshinsky got the chance to orchestrate the Trial of the Sixteen, where he undoubtedly enjoyed calling this man a "mad dog" and a "contemptible pygmy." This Old Bolshevik was executed along with his ally Lev Kamenev.

swap.leadin: She has been called "the German woman on the Czar's throne"
swap.text: Name this empress of Russia who reigned from 1762 to 1796. Like Frederick II of Prussia and Joseph II of Austria, she was referred to as an "Enlightened Despot" and corresponded with philosophes like Voltaire and Diderot.
swap.answerHtml: Catherine II [or Catherine the Great or Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst or Yekaterina Velikaya or Yekaterina Alekseyevna; prompt on “Catherine”]
swap.clue: This ruler took power in a coup against her husband Peter III.

question.leadin: Jerome Blum's book Lord and Peasant, which examines master-slave relations, was released on the hundredth anniversary of this action, which marked the end of the "forbidden years."
question.text: Name this action taken on March 3, 1861. This action was ordered by a ruler who was later assassinated by the anarchist People's Will.
question.answerHtml: emancipation of the serfs [or freeing of the serfs by Tsar Alexander II of Russia; or equivalents]
question.clue: The obrok("ah-BROKE")tax was abolished with this action, which gave the residents of mirs ("meers") voting rights with zemstvos.

swap.text: From the 2000s onwards, this leader oversaw construction of the Astravets Nuclear Power Plant. Protestors targeted this long-serving leader in the Jeans Revolution.
swap.answerHtml: Alexander Lukashenko [or Alexander Grigoryevich Lukashenko; or Alyaksandr Ryhoravich Lukashenka] (Alexander Lukashenko is the president of Belarus.)
swap.clue: During a 2006 press conference, this man claimed that he rigged the vote to lower his own totals, since it is not a European outcome.

question.text: The Estonian Civil War began when the Soviet 6th Red Rifle Division attacked this Estonian city. A Great Northern War battle named for this city that took place in a blizzard was a victory for Sweden over Peter the Great's forces.

swap.leadin: This ruler's death prompted Frederick II of Prussia to claim that "The Messalina of the North is dead. Morta la Bestia."
swap.text: Name this empress of Russia and daughter of Peter the Great. The accession of her nephew Peter III to the throne following her death became known in Prussia as the Miracle of the House of Brandenburg.

question.leadin: This man was assisted by Epifany Slavinetsky in revising several service-books that were previously modified by Joasaphus I.
question.text: Name this patriarch who was condemned by a synod called by Tsar Alexis. His reforms to church rituals caused the Raskol, in which the Old Believers broke away from the Russian Orthodox Church.
question.clue: The Old Believers split in 1666 in response to the reforms of this Patriarch. In that same year, a synod bumped him down to monk status due to the controversy of his reforms.

swap.leadin: Name these advisors to Catherine the Great.
swap.text: This final lover and favorite of Catherine was of ignoble birth and irritated his courtiers by allowing his pet monkey to steal their hats. After being exiled from court by Tsar Paul following Catherine's death, he participated in the coup against Paul.

question.text: A century earlier, this man had led a Cossack revolt against Alexei I, the second Romanov tsar. He is perhaps most notable for building a Cossack navy on the Caspian Sea, which he then sailed up the Volga.
question.clue: This rebel leader who founded a Cossack republic as part of a 1670 rebellion in which he led thousands of followers up the Volga towards Moscow.

swap.leadin: This president lost popularity after censoring media coverage concerning his negotiations over the disputed Tuzla Island.
swap.text: Give this president who pursued a dual policy of appeasing the West and Russia, known as his Multi-Vector Doctrine. This man's downfall ultimately occurred due his involvement in the assassination of journalistGeorgiy Gongadze.
